description: Male AGA Norwood 4, 42y, with ferritin deficiency (adversarial).

clinicalRationale.whyPrimary: Male, age 42, with progressive Norwood-4 pattern thinning concentrated at crown/temporal regions, family history positive, and minimal active shedding. The pattern topology (terminal-to-vellus transition without diffuse shed) is the definitional signature of androgen-driven miniaturization. Pathway activation is dominated by follicular miniaturization (≥0.60) with the telogen pathway only modestly activated, which the cause registry's log-likelihood weights resolve into a dominant posterior for androgen-driven miniaturization. The case therefore leads on the androgenic cause with the standard MPHL protocol class and Norwood-grade-locked kit gating.

whyNotCompetitors.stress-driven-telogen-effluvium: Architectural thinning without heavy diffuse shedding makes a telogen-driven explanation weaker; TE would require a synchronized precipitant and acute timing that this case does not show.
whyNotCompetitors.inflammatory-scalp-dysfunction: Normal/oily scalp without burning, pustules, or psoriatic plaques does not support inflammation as the primary explanation.
whyNotCompetitors.autoimmune-hair-loss: No patchy loss, no areata history, no scarring markers — autoimmune cause is excluded at the signal layer.
whyNotCompetitors.nutritional-hair-stress: Iron deficiency is a real co-driver but the pattern topology and grade progression cannot be explained by substrate insufficiency alone; nutrition is repleted in parallel without leading the explanation.
whyNotCompetitors.multifactorial-hair-loss: Only one or two pathways exceed 0.40 activation; compositeRule (≥3 pathways) is not satisfied so multifactorial cannot lead.

commonFailureModes.description: Iron-deficiency signal weight can push a naive Bayes ranker into nutritional cause leadership; the pattern signature must outweigh it.
